title: Transfer matrix level independence
html:
Proposition. Transfer matrix level independence

Proposition (conditional on conj:crystal-graph-realization — transfer-matrix level independence). Let \mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \oplus \mathcal{L} be a hadron with composite knot K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}. Let \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}_p) be the categorical transfer matrix (categorical transfer matrix). Then:

  1. Constituent-composite agreement. The composite invariant is derived from the constituents rather than independent of them: the Markov trace computed from the constituent insertion points (z_1, \ldots, z_n) is the composite invariant, so two hadrons with the same constituents have the same composite. Concretely,

      \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}(q)
  = 
  \hat{V}^{\mathrm{comp}}(q)
  = 
  J_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q).

  2. Path independence on \mathcal{S}_p. Two braiding operations T_1, T_2 on \mathfrak{H} that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations (isotopy equivalence) have the same categorical transfer matrix: \mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2). In particular, the specific sequence of crossing changes within the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p does not affect the result --- only the equivalence class of the final configuration matters.

  3. Well-definedness. The categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the isotopy class of the hadron \mathfrak{H} and the knot types K_i of its constituents. It is independent of:

    • the braid representative \beta_{\mathfrak{H}},
    • the PawLei embedding \iota_{j_i} for each constituent,
    • the order of crossings evaluated within \mathcal{S}_p.
